LESSON: this repo has (at least) two parallel, differently-shaped 'refusal' conventions for the SAME rail concept -- LayerAbsenceWire's {status:'absent', verdict:...} and the *FactFromParcelRecord.ts family's {state:'refused', code, reason} (ZoningFactRead, CityLimitsFactWire's cell-level refusal collapsed into status:'unmeasured'). verify-walk.mjs's classifyRequiredLeaf (reproduced verbatim in nodeFacetBakeTier1Conformant.test.ts) reads `rec.verdict ?? rec.state`, deliberately dual-shape-aware so both conventions grade correctly -- but only for the literal strings absent-verified/not-applicable/refused; any other token (lookup-failed, unmeasured, stamp-missing) on a non-empty object silently grades as state:'value'. Check which of the two shapes (and which literal verdict/state string) a given serve-boundary fix actually needs BEFORE picking a fix, not after.
